summary:
ALPHA is an offline-capable desktop application built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 that translates NASA Earth observation data into an interactive 3D crop simulator. By combining FAO-56 biophysical models with satellite baselines (SMAP, MODIS, VIIRS, NASADEM) and NASA POWER weather feeds, ALPHA models 120-day growing seasons across 13 global regions for 8 staple crops.

Through a real-time 3D field visualization, dual heatmaps, and synchronized charts, users can monitor soil health and test mid-season field interventions—such as targeted irrigation, simulated heatwaves, and crop rotation. Available in four languages with local data caching, ALPHA equips growers and researchers with intuitive tools to make proactive, climate-resilient agricultural decisions.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

ALPHA (Agrostrategic Field Intelligence) is an interactive desktop simulator that translates NASA Earth observation data into a living, 3D agricultural testbed. Users begin by selecting their preferred language (English, French, Arabic, or Spanish) and choosing one of 13 agricultural zones across seven countries—including Guinea, Senegal, Mali, Kenya, Vietnam, Brazil, and India—paired with one of eight staple crops (rice, maize, wheat, sorghum, millet, cowpea, peanut, or soybean).

Once launched, the simulation engine computes a daily 120-day growing season. It fetches historical weather analogs from NASA’s POWER API (with a built-in climatology fallback for offline use) and anchors them to satellite baselines from SMAP (soil moisture), MODIS (NDVI vegetation health), VIIRS (thermal anomalies), and NASADEM (elevation). Using the internationally recognized FAO-56 Penman-Monteith standard, ALPHA continuously models reference evapotranspiration, root-zone soil water balance, nitrogen mineralization and legume fixation, and Growing Degree Days (GDD). As the user scrubs through time, a procedural 3D field reflects the crop’s biological reality—progressing through emergence, vegetative growth, flowering, and maturity, or visibly yellowing and thinning under drought and heat stress—while synchronized 2D heatmaps and charts track soil moisture, thermal stress, NDVI, and projected yield. At any moment, users can intervene by adjusting irrigation (0–60 mm), simulating heatwaves or rainfall drops, regenerating nitrogen, or executing a live mid-season crop rotation to immediately see how those choices reshape the harvest.

Benefits & Expected Impact

Most agricultural modeling tools are either expensive, require continuous high-speed internet, or demand specialized technical training to interpret raw satellite telemetry. ALPHA removes those barriers by packaging complex biophysical science into a fast, offline-capable desktop application that anyone can navigate in seconds.

In regions vulnerable to erratic rainfall and rising temperatures—such as the Sahel, South Asia, and the Mekong Delta—testing field strategies in the real world carries high financial and food-security risks. By giving agronomists, agricultural extension workers, educators, and growers a risk-free environment to test "what-if" scenarios, ALPHA shifts decision-making from reactive crisis management to proactive planning. The expected impact is smarter water conservation, better soil nitrogen management through strategic crop rotation, and stronger crop resilience in communities on the front lines of climate variability.

Tools, Languages, Hardware & Software Used

We built ALPHA from the ground up for speed, portability, and visual responsiveness without relying on heavy third-party frameworks:

  • Languages & Core Stack: Vanilla TypeScript, HTML5/CSS3, and Vite for rapid bundling and deterministic builds.
  • Desktop Architecture: Tauri v2 (Rust-backed desktop wrapper) to compile a lightweight, native executable with local persistence via LocalStorage for preferences, API tokens, and geospatial weather caches.
  • 3D & 2D Graphics: Three.js for the procedural 3D crop field and weather effects, paired with custom-engineered HTML5 Canvas 2D pipelines for real-time soil moisture/thermal heatmaps and synchronized diagnostic charts.
  • Scientific Models & Data: FAO-56 Penman-Monteith evapotranspiration equations, GDD phenology models, and NASA Earth science datasets (NASA POWER, SMAP, MODIS, VIIRS, and NASADEM).
  • Hardware: Standard consumer laptops and desktop workstations used for 3D shader testing, agronomic validation, and cross-resolution UI profiling.

What Makes It Creative

Instead of displaying satellite metrics as static tables or abstract graphs, ALPHA turns orbital data into an intuitive, tactile experience. Combining real-time procedural 3D plant biology with live mid-season intervention replay creates an immediate cause-and-effect feedback loop: users don't just read that a 3°C heat anomaly reduces grain fill—they watch the canopy react, see the thermal heatmap shift, and test whether targeted irrigation or crop rotation can rescue the yield. Furthermore, our multi-season carry-over mechanic tracks ending soil nitrogen and crop history into subsequent seasons, encouraging long-term regenerative thinking rather than single-harvest optimization.

Key Factors Our Team Considered

  • Accessibility & Low-Connectivity Resilience: Because rural agricultural hubs often face unstable internet, we engineered an intelligent caching system with a 14-day TTL and deterministic regional climatology fallbacks so the app works reliably offline.
  • Linguistic & Cultural Inclusion: To serve diverse farming regions authentically, we integrated native, persistent support for four major languages (English, French, Arabic, and Spanish) right from the first launch screen.
  • Performance & Responsive Design: Running real-time 3D rendering alongside 120-day daily biophysical recalculations required strict optimization—precomputing daily states, avoiding bloated UI libraries, and designing a responsive layout that adapts cleanly from widescreen monitors down to compact 440px viewports.
